qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Prime central London commercial developments and dominant regional shopping destinations possess unreplicable physical locations and complex planning approvals. However, commercial real estate asset intensity results in a 10-year average ROIC of only 3.0-4.0%, failing the 12% compounding hurdle. Landsec cannot enforce pricing power above inflation without driving tenant vacancies, lease renegotiations, or retail tenant failures during consumer downturns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Flagship UK commercial property portfolio generates 10-year historical ROIC of only 3.0-4.0%, structurally trailing the 12% hurdle. Real estate rental yields cannot achieve compounding quality standards without excessive debt leverage, while London office demand and shopping center leasing face persistent tenant rationalization.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC averages in the 3.0-3.9% range, heavily affected by multi-billion-pound property revaluation deficits during UK rate-hiking cycles. Retail tenant restructuring (CVAs) and persistent hybrid working adoption across London office occupiers constrain lease renewal pricing power and cap total accounting returns.
